notes: **New shape: the support, a flat bar that stiffens the keyguard across an opening.** Unlike a ridge, a support never stands above the keyguard: it is exactly as thick as the keyguard where it lies, so on the screen area it is as thick as the screen area, and on a thicker border as thick as the border. Everywhere it meets plastic it gets fillets, at the wall of every opening it crosses and at the plastic between them, so each opening it divides keeps rounded corners like the rest. Where two supports cross, the corners where they meet are filleted too. Its top edges are beveled to match the openings around it. You can write one in screen openings, case openings or tablet openings, in `openings_and_additions.txt` or the matching "my … openings" setting, as the shape `"support"`. Its corner value is the radius of its fillets (0 for square corners). It is 2 mm wide and 10 mm long unless you give it a width and a length. Its x and y are the middle of its starting end, or its middle with the "C" anchor. It runs only across or up and down: a direction of 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees, and a support at any other angle is skipped with a warning in the console. Laser-cut keyguards get supports too. In desktop OpenSCAD, a design with a support previews about as slowly as it renders, because the support has to see the finished keyguard to know where its fillets go.

**New grid variables gl and gr: the left and right edges of the grid.** They join gw, gh, gt and gb, and are measured the same way as a screen opening's x, in millimeters or pixels as appropriate, so gr minus gl is the grid width. You can use them in `openings_and_additions.txt` and in the "my … openings" settings, for example to center an opening on the grid at x = (gl+gr)/2.

**New variable bw: the width of the bars.** It is the width the status bar, message bars and command bars are actually cut at: the app's width, less any left or right edge compensation for tight cases that reaches past the case border. Like the other app variables it is in millimeters or pixels as appropriate, and you can use it in `openings_and_additions.txt` and in the "my … openings" settings.

The designer now tells the Keyguard Designer web app where the middle of the grid is, so that **Snap** on its “by eye” tab can line openings up with it. Nothing about the keyguard changes, and there is nothing different to see in OpenSCAD.
